title: Coherence of the finite Tate-source structural comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Work on the small pro-etale derived categories with $A=A_{E,n}$ and the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated and finite type between such schemes, with geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Write $F_f=Lf^*$, $T_{r,X}=A_X(r)$, and $P_fK=(F_fK\otimes^L T_{d,X})[2d]$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ write $c_f:G_XF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fG_Y$ for the canonical commuting-pullback comparison and
$$b_{f,K}=(c_{f,K}\otimes1)[2d]\,\mu_{g_X;F_fK,T_{d,X}}[2d]:G_XP_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_fG_YK\otimes^LG_XT_{d,X})[2d],$$
where $\mu$ is the canonical pullback-tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], as in [def-pur-tate-datum]. Let $Q_X,Q_Y$ be either derived reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$, $1\le m\le n$, on $X,Y$, or $Lu^*,Lv^*$ for the geometric base change of a Cartesian square of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes with vertical arrows $f_0,f'_0$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Denote the target coefficient/scheme objects by primes; put $K'=Q_YK$, and let $C_T:Q_TG_T\cong G'_TQ_T$ be the canonical comparison. Let $a_P:Q_XP_fK\cong P'_{f'}K'$ be the canonical pullback, tensor, twist and shift comparison. Put $H_fK=(F_fG_YK\otimes^LG_XT_{d,X})[2d]$. Let $a_H:Q_XH_fK\cong H'_{f'}K'$ be obtained from the same comparisons, using $C_Y$ on the input factor and $G'_X(t)C_X$ on the twist factor, where $t:Q_XT_{d,X}\cong T'_{d,X'}$. Then
$$a_H Q_X(b_{f,K})=b'_{f',K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
For composable smooth geometric base changes $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$, the two canonical expansions of $G_X(P_fP_hK)$ to the shifted tensor of $F_fF_hG_ZK$, $G_XF_fT_{e,Y}$ and $G_XT_{d,X}$ agree: expanding $b_f$ and $F_f(b_h)$ gives the same map as expanding $b_{hf}$ and then the pullback, tensor and twist-additivity identifications, where $e$ is the pure relative dimension of $h$. The comparison is natural in $K$, uses canonical composition maps, and commutes with the termwise shift identifications. Reduction is restricted to the finite-Tor domains of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The pullback-composition comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

proof.text: First suppress the shifts. Write $L=T_{d,X}$, $M=F_fK$, and $\bar b_f=(c_f\otimes1)\mu_{g_X;M,L}$. The canonical tensor comparisons and pullback compositors are the normalized ones, not chosen objectwise isomorphisms: on flat-term K-flat models they are ordinary balanced tensor maps. In particular the tensor map splits $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ as $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, while collapsing two pullbacks multiplies their scalar factors. The cited ambient coherence statement gives associative compositors and their monoidality at a fixed finite coefficient ring. Thus a comparison between two equal composite scheme maps, obtained by one compositor followed by the inverse of another, is monoidal too. The finite derived normalization supplies the corresponding balanced coefficient-change square, without requiring a quotient coefficient ring to be flat. These facts apply in the ambient unbounded module derived categories, hence to every object in the finite-Tor domains in the question.

proof.text:
Put $q_{U,V}:Q_X(U\otimes^LV)\cong Q_XU\otimes^LQ_XV$. In either case the specified comparison $C_X:Q_XG_X\cong G'_XQ_X$ is monoidal, in the precise form
$$(C_{X,U}\otimes C_{X,V})q_{G_XU,G_XV}Q_X(\mu_{g_X;U,V})=\mu_{g'_X;Q_XU,Q_XV}G'_X(q_{U,V})C_{X,U\otimes^LV}.$$
For reduction this is the coefficient square in the finite derived normalization, with $u=g_X$ and $C_X=\kappa^{-1}$; invert its displayed scalar-association comparison and rearrange. For geometric pullback, substitute $Q_X=Lu^*$ and $u g'_X=g_Xu$; apply the tensor-compositor equation to the two paths $u,g_X$ and $g'_X,u$, and cancel the common tensor comparison of their composite. This gives exactly the displayed equation, since $C_X$ is the comparison of those paths. All rearrangements use invertible maps, and both equations are natural in $U,V$.

proof.text:
Let $\sigma_K:Q_XF_fK\cong F'_{f'}Q_YK$ be the canonical comparison of the square or of coefficient extension. The commuting input comparisons satisfy
$$F'_{f'}(C_{Y,K})\,\sigma_{G_YK}\,Q_X(c_{f,K})=c'_{f',Q_YK}\,G'_X(\sigma_K)\,C_{X,F_fK}.$$
For geometric pullback, expand each commuting-square comparison as two compositors; apply the cited associativity equality to each triple in the cube $f u=v f'$, $f g_X=g_Y f$, $u g'_X=g_Xu$, $v g'_Y=g_Yv$. Cancel adjacent inverse compositors. Both paths become the comparison from pullback along $f u g'_X=g_Y v f'$ to $F'_{f'}G'_YQ_Y$, so they agree. For reduction use a flat-term K-flat representative of $K$. The specified compositors are its termwise module pullback maps, and $\sigma,C$ are the balanced scalar-association maps. After collapsing the nested pullbacks, both paths send a generalized pure tensor with scalar factors $a,b$ to the pulled-back section multiplied by $\bar a\bar b=\overline{ab}$. Inserting units gives the same inverse maps. Thus these are equal chain maps, and their classes give the displayed derived equality. This computation uses the representative normalizations in the cited statements, so it proves equality for the actual canonical comparisons and every $K$.

proof.text:
Write $F'=F'_{f'}$, $G'=G'_X$, and $t:Q_XL\cong L'$. Without shifts the comparisons in the question are
$$\bar a_P=(\sigma_K\otimes t)q_{M,L},\qquad \bar a_H=(F'C_{Y,K}\,\sigma_{G_YK}\otimes G'(t)C_{X,L})q_{F_fG_YK,G_XL}.$$
Expand $\bar a_HQ_X(\bar b_f)$. Naturality of $q$ moves $Q_X(c_f\otimes1)$ through it, giving the tensor product of $F'C_Y\,\sigma_{G_YK}\,Q_Xc_f$ and $G'(t)C_{X,L}$ after $q_{G_XM,G_XL}Q_X\mu_{g_X;M,L}$. Substitute Step 3 in the first factor. Substitute Step 2 in the remaining tensor comparison. Finally naturality of $\mu_{g'_X}$ for the pair $(\sigma_K,t)$ moves $G'(\sigma_K)\otimes G'(t)$ to its input. The resulting expression is
$$(c'_{f',K'}\otimes1)\mu_{g'_X;F'K',L'}G'((\sigma_K\otimes t)q_{M,L})C_{X,M\otimes L}=\bar b'_{f',K'}G'(\bar a_P)C_{X,M\otimes L}.$$
This proves the unshifted square. Only bifunctoriality and naturality are used beyond the equations proved in Steps 2 and 3; in particular the argument works for the given twist isomorphism $t$ itself.

proof.text: For composition put $U=F_fF_hK$, $V=F_fT_{e,Y}$, $W=T_{d,X}$. The cited twist-pullback identification and the definition by nonnegative tensor powers identify $V\otimes^LW$ with $T_{d+e,X}$ by reassociating the $e+d$ copies of the degree-zero Tate line (and the unit when $d=0$ or $e=0$). Expand both proposed maps with target $((F_fF_hG_ZK\otimes G_XV)\otimes G_XW)[2(d+e)]$. Ignoring shifts for the moment, a common expression is: first split $G_X((U\otimes V)\otimes W)$ by two applications of $\mu_{g_X}$; then apply $(F_f(c_{h,K})c_{f,F_hK})\otimes1\otimes1$. To obtain this expression from $b_f$ followed by $F_f(b_h)$, use monoidality of $c_f$ to distribute it across $F_hK\otimes T_{e,Y}$, use compatibility of $\mu$ with pullback composition, and use $c_{f,T_{e,Y}}^{-1}$ on the second factor to express it as $G_XV$. To obtain it from $b_{hf}$, use the compositor associativity equality to replace $c_{hf}$ on the first factor by $F_f(c_h)c_f$, and use naturality of $\mu$ on the twist-additivity isomorphism $V\otimes W\cong T_{d+e,X}$. Associativity of $\mu$ identifies the two ways of splitting the triple tensor. Thus both maps are the displayed common expression. The only facts used here are the stated tensor/compositor laws; twist additivity for $d,e\ge0$ is the elementary reassociation of their defining powers.

proof.text: Restore shifts using the canonical termwise comparisons. The cited pullback-tensor shift theorem identifies the tensor comparison before and after a shift of either input. The compositor is termwise on the same flat-term K-flat model, so shifting it gives the compositor on the shifted model; the balanced coefficient maps likewise do not change cochain degree. The signed tensor-shift maps have coefficient $(-1)^{bp}$ on the summand of first-factor degree $p$. Consequently the shift extractions used in composition, with $b=2d$ or $2e$, have coefficient $1$; their addition law identifies both targets with shift $[2(d+e)]$. Localizing these termwise identifications gives precisely $a_HQ_X(b_{f,K})=b'_{f',K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}$ and the claimed composite equality. Naturality in $K$ follows because every comparison used above is natural, including the representative normalizations; the same reasoning commutes with every termwise shift identification. Finally retain exactly the finite-Tor restriction of the cited reduction theorem; the argument uses its pullback and tensor comparisons only and never asserts flatness of $A_{E,m}$ over $A_{E,n}$.
